payload.rationale: Read-through cache of the resolved link (positive + short negative TTL): removes the DB from the hot path; negative caching blunts enumeration; Invalidate on PATCH/DELETE: correctness over hit rate for state changes; Per API key for writes, per client IP for redirects: fairness for authenticated clients, abuse protection for public traffic; 429 with Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers: standard, client-friendly back-off signal; Per-app CollectorRegistry: isolated in tests, no global state; p95 < 50 ms @ 20 concurrent clients (laptop, SQLite) enforced as a gate: a concrete, repeatable number replaces 'faster'; Opaque random keys hashed with SHA-256 (keys have 256 bits of entropy, so a slow KDF adds nothing): fast verification on every write without storing secrets; Owner-only PATCH/DELETE: prevents one tenant modifying another tenant's links
One protocol, two backends: the in-memory LRU keeps the single-process default dependency-free, Redis shares state across replicas. Values are small JSON strings; TTLs are enforced per entry.
Token buckets allow short bursts while bounding sustained rate. The Redis variant runs the read-modify-write in a Lua script so concurrent replicas cannot double-spend tokens.
Labels use the route template (/{code}), never the raw path, so cardinality stays bounded. A per-app CollectorRegistry avoids global state and duplicate-registration errors in tests.

Turns "faster" into a measurable, repeatable number. Links are seeded through the service layer, the server runs as a separate process, and each concurrent worker owns its own HTTP connection so the measurement is not dominated by client-side connection-pool contention.
